p: This is a family arcade built for fun, flashing lights and prize tickets rather than anything grown-up, so it's a straightforward pick for kids' birthdays and school-holiday outings. Because it runs on cash here rather than a top-up card, a good tip is to split your spending money into envelopes or pockets for each child before you arrive. When their pot's gone, it's gone, and everyone knows where they stand.

Braehead sits on the south bank of the River Clyde in Renfrew, handy for the M8 and only a few minutes from Glasgow Airport. That makes it easy to reach by car from across the west of Scotland, and it's popular with families visiting from Paisley, Renfrewshire and the city itself. The shopping centre next door gives you food courts, cafés and plenty of shops, so a trip can easily mix errands with a bit of fun.

If you're keen to pack more in, the Clyde is lined with big family attractions within a short drive. The Riverside Museum, with its trams, cars and old Glasgow street, and the Glasgow Science Centre are both brilliant rainy-day picks, and the tall ship Glenlee is moored right outside the Riverside Museum. Arrive with a rough plan for the day, give the kids a time limit in the arcade and you'll avoid the classic "five more minutes" standoff. Weekday afternoons outside the school holidays tend to be calmer if your little ones prefer a bit more space.
